mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D (1GD-FTV) engine replacement typically costs £5,500-£7,100 for a rebuilt unit, £4,342-£5,500 for reconditioned, and £2,000-£3,500 for a used engine. Supply and fit adds approximately £1,000-£1,500 depending on the specialist and your location. Rebuilt engines include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty. Used engines are the cheapest option but carry higher risk. The Land Cruiser's value retention makes replacement economically viable in most cases.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of DPF failure in a Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include a warning light on the dashboard, excessive white smoke from the exhaust, reduced performance, increased fuel consumption, and frequent regeneration cycles. Toyota has acknowledged repeated problems with the DPF system fitted to 1GD-FTV engines. DPF cleaning costs £250-£400 at specialist rates. Delaying repair can cause turbocharger or engine damage. Regular long journeys help prevent DPF blockages.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical 2015-2025 Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D retains value exceptionally well, with examples ranging from £25,000-£60,000. With a rebuilt engine costing £5,500-£7,100, replacement is almost always worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise in good condition. Replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. Rebuilt engines come with a 12-month warranty for peace of mind. Land Cruisers are known for longevity - a replacement engine can extend life significantly.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical engine replacement on a Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D takes 2-3 working days for supply and fit through a specialist. Used engines may be available faster if already in stock; rebuilt engines typically require longer lead times. Most specialists offer next-day or 48-hour delivery on used units. Rebuilt engines typically require 5-7 working days. The 1GD-FTV is a complex modern diesel requiring specialist fitting.

mainEntity.name: What is the engine code for the Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D uses the 1GD-FTV engine code - a 2.8-litre four-cylinder turbocharged diesel from Toyota's GD engine family. It was introduced in 2015 as a replacement for the 3.0-litre 1KD-FTV and offers 25 per cent more torque with 15 per cent better fuel economy. 1GD-FTV is the sole engine code for the Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D. Always verify your engine code using your V5C registration document. The engine meets Euro 6 emissions standards with urea-SCR NOx reduction.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: All engines supplied through EnginesMarket carry a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Rebuilt and reconditioned units offer comprehensive cover including parts and labour. 12-month warranty covers parts and labour on rebuilt engines. Always confirm exact terms with your chosen supplier. Some suppliers offer extended warranties for Land Cruiser engines due to their value.

historyTimeline.h2: Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D was introduced to the UK market in summer 2015 as a direct replacement for the long-serving 3.0-litre 1KD-FTV engine. The new 1GD-FTV engine represented a significant technological leap, featuring world-first Thermo Swing Wall Insulation Technology and achieving 44 per cent thermal efficiency - making it one of the most thermally efficient diesel engines on the market. Despite its smaller displacement, the 2.8 D-4D offered 25 per cent more torque than its predecessor, with 11 per cent more torque available at low revs and a 15 per cent improvement in fuel economy.

milestones.description: 1GD-FTV 2.8-litre D-4D turbodiesel makes UK debut in the Land Cruiser; 177 PS (174 bhp) version with 450 Nm torque introduced
Engine rollout expands to Hilux and other Toyota models
Higher-output 204 PS (150 kW) version introduced with 500 Nm torque
J250 series Land Cruiser launched with updated 2.8 D-4D producing 204 PS and 500 Nm, paired with eight-speed automatic transmission
2024 (facelift) - 70 Series facelift debuts with 150 kW (204 PS) 2.8 D-4D producing 500 Nm from 600-2,800 rpm

commonProblems.h2: Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D's 1GD-FTV engine represents a significant step forward in diesel technology, but like all modern common-rail diesels, it has its weak points. DPF blockages, injector wear, and turbocharger faults are the most common reasons for replacement enquiries. Rebuilt Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF Blockage & Regeneration Issues - Why the Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D 1GD-FTV Suffers Exhaust System Problems
problems.affectedModels: Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D (1GD-FTV, 2015-present, particularly 2015-2020 models)
problems.rootCause: The diesel particulate filter (DPF) system on early 1GD-FTV engines can become blocked, particularly in vehicles used predominantly for stop-start urban driving rather than longer journeys. Toyota has acknowledged repeated problems with the DPF system fitted to 1GD-FTV engines. Issues stem from under-enthusiastic regeneration cycles and, in some cases, a fifth injector that can jam. A class action highlighted excessive white smoke due to DPF problems.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Professional DPF cleaning, forced regeneration cycle
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early before permanent filter damage
Best if filter is beyond cleaning or physically damaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if DPF issues have caused wider engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2015-2025 Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D retains value exceptionally well, with examples ranging from £25,000-£60,000 depending on age, mileage and specification. With the vehicle firmly in the £25,000+ bracket, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine replacement is almost always justified by the premium via warranty and reliability.
problems.recommendation: DPF issues are often preventable with regular long journeys and proper maintenance. If you catch problems early (warning lights, reduced performance), a professional DPF clean or forced regeneration is the most cost-effective solution. For vehicles used predominantly in urban environments, consider a full DPF replacement with updated components. Engine replacement is rarely necessary for DPF issues alone.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 1GD-FTV Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D engine prices

problems.h4: Injector Wear & Fuel System Issues - Why the Toyota Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D 1GD-FTV Suffers Common-Rail Problems
problems.rootCause: The 1GD-FTV's common-rail fuel injection system uses four injectors that can wear or leak over time, particularly with poor fuel quality or infrequent filter changes. Injector issues can cause rough running, smoke, loss of power, and fuel dilution of engine oil.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all four injectors, code to ECU, reset adaptations
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught before piston or cylinder damage occurs
Best if injector failure has caused piston or cylinder damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - a typical Land Cruiser 2.8 D-4D sits in the £25,000-£60,000 bracket. For a vehicle in this range, injector replacement or full engine replacement both make financial sense, depending on the extent of damage.
problems.recommendation: Injector failure is one of the most common maintenance items on the 1GD-FTV. If diagnosed early (rough idle, smoke, hard starting), injector replacement is the right call. If the vehicle has been driven with failing injectors causing piston damage, a rebuilt engine is the only reliable solution.
